questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses that the school offered, that it was an english speaking destination and the experience of a "university city"/college town

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Dartmouth was generally very helpful in providing information, but it was very unclear if I as an exchange student where supposed to participate in the introduction week for Freshmen. It was nice being there for a week before classes started, but mostly because some of the other Danes also had arrived, otherwise it would have been very lonely.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The other Danes helped me find my room and show me the whereabouts

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I was very surprised to find out that it is mandatory to live on campus in one of the dorms. I spent a lot of time trying to find housing, before I found out that I was obligated to live in one of the dorms, and that Dartmouth "provided" (at an expensive price) a room for me. This information would have been nice to know before applying. All in all, it was nice to live on campus and it made it less stressful that all housing matters where sorted through the institution.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You are obligated to join the Ivy-unlimited mealplan. It is quite costly, but very convenient to have a full buffet at your disposal almost 24/7 and never having to do grocery shopping og cleaning dishes. As the work load is heavy at Dartmouth this was very helpful

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That Dartmouth provides a dorm room for you and that you are not guaranteed to get you own private room (luckily I did).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There are a lot of different websites and mailing systems that you need to orient yourself in. But as long as you keep yourself updated (very important) and check your e-mails it was "easy" enough

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could always get ahold of student service at Dartmouth through e-mail, and they where very responsive and helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep yourself updated and regularly check your emails

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Even as a MA student you are only able to attend BA courses at the institution. This did not affect my merits at my home institution. 
One very important thing to be aware of is that in the fall-term you are only able to do three courses of 22,5 ECTS points, as the term at Dartmouth are only 10 weeks.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had a way bigger work load throughout the term. You have more assignments, tests, presentations, papers, midterms etc. It is also more expected of you that you read all of the curriculum, as there are higher expectations for participation. I didn't have any lectures, but only class-based courses. I will say though that I have rarely learned so much in such a short span of time. You get way closer with your professors and are a more active part of class discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Elections and Reform
Intro to Middle East Politics
COCO26 what's in your toolbox

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: the coco26 is a course specially designed for exchange students. You visit museums, watch plays and generally debate how it is to be a responsible traveler in a globalised world.

You are obligated to buy their insurance (even though my private one had a bigger coverage)
The Ivy-unlimites mealplan was unexpected, but turned out to be worth the money and a big part of the college experience

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The meal-plan, a dorm room and the insurance

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything! Not kidding, and all activities are part of your tuition. The only problem is that I felt like I didn't have enough time for it all!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Canooing at the Conneticut river, watching sports games (especially ice-hockey, volleyball and rowing was fun to watch), using the creative spaces for crafts making, going to the climbing hall, joining the outings clubs trips into the mountains

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The surrounding nature, sports games and Fraternity parties

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy as it is a small space and people are extremely welcoming and friendly

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in the events that the school provide!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The age difference as I'm a 26 year old MA student and this was 19 year old freshmen. My stay wouldn't have been the same if it wasn't for the six other Danish exchange student. We where good at socialising with the Americans (going on runs, trips and to parties), but the Danes where definitely my closest friends at the stay

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How welcoming and embracing the other students where. I got a lot of American friends and contacts while I was there

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The fall term is only 22,5 ECTS point
That housing, meal-plans and insurance are mandatory and quite expensive (but it makes it that much easier!)
To remember to enjoy some of all the free activities (I wish I had spend a bit less time in the study halls and more time on activities and outings)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: all public transportation in Hanover is free:)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Meeting all these wonderful people (both Danish and American), and experiencing a very intense, but instructive academic environment.
Experiencing the election first hand and the political debate (even in the light of the very depressing results)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had to go to the hospital and the insurance situaiton afterwards was a hard process.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
